sections.h2: Where is a deed recorded when you sell a house in Ionia County?
sections.html:
Every deed for land in Ionia County is recorded by the county Register of Deeds, and the recording is what puts a sale on the public record. The office accepts documents in person, by mail, or through an approved electronic recording provider. Staff will not help you draft or fix a document, so the paperwork should arrive finished, usually from a title company or an attorney.

Ionia County covers about 571 square miles of land, and the county seat is the city of Ionia. The county sits inside the Grand Rapids area, which means many sellers here deal with buyers who commute west. If you are selling a house in Ionia County, the deed you sign at closing is the document this office stamps, indexes and files.

Walk-in recordings are handed back right away. Mailed documents come back only if you enclose a self-addressed stamped envelope, and the office holds anything sent without one for 90 days. You can reach the office at (616) 527-5320 or deeds@ioniacounty.org.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Ionia County?
sections.html:
The flat charge is $30 per document, however many pages it runs. The county accepts cash, check or card, and a card payment carries a service fee that depends on the amount charged. Recording fees and transfer tax can go on a single check.

ItemAmount
Recording fee, any deed or mortgage$30.00 per document
Extra charge when one document assigns or discharges several instruments$3.00 for each additional instrument
Tax certification from the County Treasurer (warranty deeds, land contracts)$5.00
Staff name search$5.00
Copies$1.00 per page
Certification of a copy$5.00 extra

Source: Ionia County Register of Deeds pages on recording fees and on document searching and copies.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax is due on an Ionia County sale?
sections.html:
Ionia County lists two taxes due at recording on any deed that sells or transfers real estate: $3.75 for each $500 of value (or fraction of $500) for the state, and $0.55 for each $500 for the county. On a $200,000 sale that works out to $1,500 state plus $220 county, or $1,720 in all. That figure is an illustration of the rates, so confirm the exact amount with your closing agent.

Michigan law carves out exemptions, and the exemption has to be written on the face of the deed. Two differ between the state and county lists, which matters for family transfers:

  • The state act (MCL 207.526) exempts a conveyance from an individual to a child, stepchild, grandchild or adopted child, and any transfer given in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure of a mortgage.
  • The county act (MCL 207.505) exempts instruments where the consideration is under $100, deeds given as security, leases, and court orders that do not name a price. It does not repeat the child and grandchild exemption.
  • Both acts exempt a land contract where title does not pass until the contract price is fully paid.

Because of those differences, a gift to a child can owe county tax and no state tax. Ask the Register of Deeds how a specific transfer is treated before you sign.

sections.h2: Which Ionia County documents need a treasurer's tax certification?
sections.html:
Warranty deeds, any deed with a covenant of warranty, land contracts and land contract assignments need a Tax Certification from the Ionia County Treasurer before the Register of Deeds will record them. The $5 certification fee can be folded into the same check as the recording fee. A quitclaim deed carries no covenant of warranty, so it generally skips this step, though the office can confirm for your particular document.

Tell your closing agent early if you owe back taxes on the parcel, because the treasurer's certification is part of the recording package. Ask the County Treasurer what the office needs before it will issue one.

sections.h2: What mistakes get a deed rejected in Ionia County?
sections.html:
The office checks every document against the Michigan recording statute (MCL 565.201 and related sections). A deed that misses a requirement is returned, which can delay a closing by days. The county publishes this checklist of common problems:

  • Signatures must be original, in black or dark blue ink, with each name typed or printed beneath.
  • The notary acknowledgment must match the printed names and carry the notary's printed name on the same page as the signature.
  • The grantee's street or post office address must appear, and the drafter's name and address must be on the document.
  • The first page needs a margin of at least 2 1/2 inches at the top and 1/2 inch on the other sides.
  • The first line of print must state the recordable event, and one document may cover only one such event.
  • Text must be black, at least 10 point, on white paper no lighter than 20 pound, between 8 1/2 by 11 and 8 1/2 by 14 inches.
  • If a deed conveys to a survivor, a certified death certificate must be recorded with it or earlier.
  • The total property value must be on the face of the deed, or a transfer tax valuation affidavit must be attached.

sections.h2: How do I search Ionia County land records?
sections.html:
The Public Workstations in the Register of Deeds office are free for searching by grantor or grantee, and copies are $1 a page. A search by legal description or parcel number at those workstations costs $1 per minute. If you ask staff to look up your latest deed, the charge is $5 plus the copy fee, and that lookup is by name only, not by property.

From home you have two options. Tapestry is a pay-per-search service at $8.95 per search, suited to a one-time look. Laredo is a monthly subscription for people who search often, such as agents and investors; call the office to open an account. For a full ownership history on a house you plan to sell, a title company search goes deeper than either.

sections.h2: What does the Ionia County housing market look like for sellers?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table shows 66,557 residents in Ionia County in July 2025, down 0.4 percent from the 2020 base. Owner-occupied homes make up 77.3 percent of housing, and the median value of those homes for 2020 to 2024 is $198,500. Median household income is $75,611, the highest of the four Michigan counties in this batch.

Commute time stands out: the mean trip to work is 27.1 minutes, longer than Isabella, Iosco or Jackson counties. Median gross rent is $884. Building permits totaled 100 in 2025, so new construction is thin and existing houses carry most of the supply. A buyer will compare your house against that thin new-build supply.

sections.h2: What happens to property taxes after an Ionia County sale?
sections.html:
A sale resets the taxable value. Under Michigan's Proposal A, a transfer of ownership uncaps the property's taxable value in the calendar year after the transfer, so the buyer's bill can jump toward the house's assessed value. Michigan Treasury lists the Property Transfer Affidavit (Form 2766) for the buyer to file with the local assessor. Ask the assessor for your city or township for the filing deadline.

Exempt transfers listed in section 211.27a(7) of the General Property Tax Act do not uncap. For questions about who bills the property, the township or city treasurer handles current taxes and the County Treasurer takes over delinquent ones.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a deed in Ionia County?
faqs.a: $30 per document, regardless of page count. If one document assigns or discharges more than one instrument number, add $3 for each additional instrument. Transfer tax and the $5 treasurer certification can be paid on the same check.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed by email in Ionia County?
faqs.a: No. The Register of Deeds does not record documents sent by email. Electronic filing goes through accredited servicers named on the county page, including Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, EPN and CSC, and only an original signed document may be scanned.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when a house sells in Ionia County?
faqs.a: The tax is due at recording, and the county page does not assign it to buyer or seller. Check the purchase agreement for who covers it, and have your closing agent show the figure on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Do I get a new deed when I pay off my mortgage in Ionia County?
faqs.a: No new deed is issued. Your lender records a discharge of mortgage, and recording a discharge costs $30, with $3 for each extra instrument it covers. Your original deed stays as the record of ownership.

faqs.q: Is a quitclaim deed to a family member taxed in Ionia County?
faqs.a: It can be taxed at the county level. State law exempts conveyances to a child or grandchild, but the county exemption list does not include them. The exemption must be stated on the deed, so ask the Register of Deeds before you record.
